# Ball joints and control arms

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Hammer the knuckle while pressure is applied to loosen the ball joint. [t1380]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Lift the lower control arm or hub with a jack to change the joint angle.
2. Hammer the knuckle while pressure is applied to loosen the ball joint.

_Procedure reported by [t1380]._

## Tools

- Jack [t1380]
- [Partial] Piece of wood (optional) [t1380]
- 4 lb. hammer [t1380]

## Tips & gotchas

- Bang the lower control arm upwards with three good whacks. [t1380]
- [Partial] Use a tie rod separator nudged between the knuckle and lower control arm. [t1380]

## Common mistakes

- Nicking, bending, or damaging the Lower Control Arm (LCA) during removal. [t1380]
